Your Almost Everything Store

Home cookin’ right off the river — and a gas station out front. If you’re looking for breakfast, lunch, or dinner, you can stop by Roy’s and get some of the best food in the area, fill up at the pumps, and pick up groceries, hardware, and gear for the river, all in one stop.

Yes — we’re a gas station, too

Gas & diesel at the pumps out front, open every day from 6:00 AM. Fill up the truck, the boat tank, and yourself — then head for the river.

One stop, half an hour from anywhere

Roy’s sits on Highway 181 in Dora, about a half-hour from any larger store — so it carries a little of everything the neighborhood and the river crowd might need. As the folks who run it like to say, you can walk in and get a chainsaw, a cold drink, and a hot meal in the same trip.

Gas Station — Gas & Diesel

Roy’s is a working gas station, not just a store with a pump. Fuel up before you head out — it’s the stop for drivers, farmers, and river traffic passing through Dora.

Groceries & Sundries

Food staples, snacks, and fountain drinks — the everyday basics, plus the thing you forgot on the way to the river.

Hardware & Chainsaw Parts

Hardware and chainsaw parts for the folks who work the land around Ozark County — because the nearest big store is a drive.

Fishing & Hunting Gear

Seasonal gear for the North Fork River crowd — tackle, supplies, and provisions for float trips and fishing days.

The Roy’s Menu

Breakfast, lunch, and dinner served daily in the dining room out back — inside and outside seating, and a daily special on the board. And whatever you do, save room for pie.

More than merchandise

Roy’s is where Dora gathers. Farmers, floaters, quilters, and pickers all end up at the same tables — visitors are warmly welcomed right alongside the regulars.

Weekly · evenings

The Music Jam

Once a week the back room fills up before 6 p.m. for a music jam — country, bluegrass, and gospel tunes. Bring an instrument if you play, or just pull up a chair and listen.

Tuesdays

Quilters’ Day

Local quilters meet at the store on Tuesdays — the same day the fresh pies usually land. Pie and quilting: it’s a whole scene, in the best way.

Now & then

Live Bands & Big Tables

The dining room — with more tables in the room tacked onto the back — hosts live bands from time to time, and a steady stream of neighbors every day in between.

Visit the Ozarks

There are plenty of other great things to do in and around Dora than just see us. Roy’s is the last stop before the North Fork River — stock up on gear, snacks, and a hot meal, then make a real trip of it: floating, fishing, and spring-fed water under the bluffs.

Check the latest from the Missouri Department of Conservation on fishing in the area before you go, and if you want the full story of the store itself, Ozarks Alive came out and wrote it up: “More than merchandise at Roy’s Store.”

Come see us

We’re on State Highway 181 in Dora — you can’t miss the store. Kitchen serves breakfast, lunch, and dinner daily.
